citation: "Therapeutic and Adverse Effects of Lasers in Dentistry: A Systematic Review," Photonics, 2023 (doi:10.3390/photonics10060650)
laser_device: multiple dental lasers reviewed (CO2, diode, Nd:YAG, Er:YAG, Argon, Erbium)
hazard_studied: adverse effects of laser use in dentistry linked to non-targeted device choice and inadequate learning curve; thermal damage to pulp tissue; cracks/fractures in composite restorations
parameter_or_operator_factor: device/wavelength selection and operator learning curve (technique-driven risk); specific power/speed values not given in abstract
adverse_outcome: cracks/fractures affecting composite restorations; thermal damage to pulp tissue in periodontal treatments; treatment failures
relevance_to_project: Systematic review synthesizing reported thermal and mechanical adverse effects of dental lasers tied to device selection and operator learning curve, useful for framing known hazard categories relevant to diode-laser soft-tissue procedure reliability.

citation: "Effect of diode lasers with wavelength of 445 and 980 nm on a temperature rise when uncovering implants for second stage surgery - an ex-vivo study in pigs," Advances in Clinical and Experimental Medicine, 2017 (doi:10.17219/acem/68943)
laser_device: 445 nm diode laser and 980 nm diode laser (comparator)
hazard_studied: thermal rise at the dental implant surface/collar during soft-tissue uncovering (second-stage implant surgery)
parameter_or_operator_factor: power (2-3 W), wavelength, contact vs. non-contact mode, fiber diameter, power density
adverse_outcome: mean temperature rises of 16.9C, 36.1C, and 21.6C measured across the three parameter groups, indicating parameter-dependent thermal risk
relevance_to_project: Closely analogous ex-vivo diode-laser design directly linking power/wavelength/contact-mode settings to measured thermal output near tissue/implant, a strong methodological parallel for a diode-laser oral soft-tissue preset/power/speed reliability study.

citation: "The Impact of Laser Thermal Effect on Histological Evaluation of Oral Soft Tissue Biopsy: Systematic Review," Dentistry Journal, 2023 (doi:10.3390/dj11020028)
laser_device: multiple wavelengths reviewed, including CO2, diode (940-980 nm and 808/445 nm), Er:YAG, Nd:YAG, KTP, and Er,Cr:YSGG lasers
hazard_studied: thermal artifact/damage affecting histological evaluation of oral soft-tissue biopsy specimens
parameter_or_operator_factor: laser wavelength/type; specific power or speed values not given in the provided abstract excerpt
adverse_outcome: thermal effects on biopsy specimens compromising histological interpretation (extent varies by wavelength per included studies)
relevance_to_project: Directly on-topic systematic review of laser thermal effects on oral soft-tissue biopsy histology/specimen quality across wavelengths including diode, core to the project's specimen-quality concern.

citation: "Thermal effect of a 445 nm diode laser on five dental implant systems: an in vitro study," Scientific Reports, 2021 (doi:10.1038/s41598-021-99709-8)
hazard_studied: thermal effect / temperature rise on dental implant systems during laser use (e.g., decontamination of ailing implants)
parameter_or_operator_factor: power (W), exposure time, mode (continuous wave vs. pulsed), contact vs. non-contact, duty cycle
adverse_outcome: temperature increases exceeding 10C at or above 0.8 W (CW, 5 s) and at 3 W pulsed (20 s, 10% duty cycle); authors concluded the laser is not inherently safe for ailing-implant decontamination under tested conditions
relevance_to_project: Strong direct precedent: controlled in vitro diode-laser study (2880 temperature curves) directly linking power/exposure-time/mode settings to thermal hazard, closely supporting the project's preset/power/speed reliability framework.
